newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German industrial output falls 1.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German industrial output falls 1.8 percent.

text.p: German industrial output fell 1.8 percent in September from the previous month, the first decline since February, the economics ministry said on Monday.
The September data are likely to be revised upward, however, it said.
"Experience shows the preliminary September data will be corrected upward significantly," the ministry said in a statement.
Production in west Germany declined 1.4 percent, while in east Germany it declined 3.4 percent.

Economist Norbert Braems at Barclays de Zoete Wedd in Frankfurt said, "It is hard to say anything on the basis of this data. It will probably be revised substantially, and the final number will probably be much higher."
Data for August were revised downward to show production unchanged from the previous month, after initial reports of a 0.8 percent gain.

Analyst Stephen King at James Capel in London said that while manufacturing production was down, a continued gain in orders suggested the inventory and export-led recovery in output should continue into the fourth quarter.

"This release is consistent with a policy of no change in interest rates," King wrote in a faxed commentary on the data. "It provides a timely reminder of some of the dangers to growth next year, as fiscal tightening takes hold."
